text:
The biggest story around James Hagens right now is that he isn't playing. The Bruins put him on injured reserve after he took a cross-check in their November 5 win in Pittsburgh, and theScore reported he will be out "a few weeks."

It interrupts one of the best rookie starts in the league. The seventh overall pick in 2025 has 6 goals and 12 points in 17 games, and as of November 3 his six goals led all rookies, per Jesse Granger of The Athletic. Among forwards picked fifth to ninth since 2005, the median first full season was 0.4 points a game. The 20-year-old is well clear of that.

Some of it will cool. He is shooting 17.6%, and Boston has scored 5.59 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. But the process is sound: at five on five the Bruins get 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances, for and against) with him out there, better than without him, and our estimate of his true scoring rate sits above the league average for a forward. When he returns, the question is whether his minutes grow to match.
headline: James Hagens was rolling. Now Boston waits.
